item.title: Introduction to machine learning
item.description:
Introduction to machine learning#

Today#

  1. What machine learning is, and why we need it; 2. Representation, evaluation, optimisation; 3. Words, notation and matrix algebra; 4. Types of machine learning; 5. Statistical learning: estimating \(f\); 6. Assessing model accuracy; 7. The bias–variance trade-off; 8. Classification: Bayes classifier and KNN

The plan for the second half of the lecture. Items 5–8 are the core of ISLP Chapter 2 and are used in every later lecture. Item 3 sets out the words and symbols of the whole course, so that no later slide uses a term that has not been defined.

item.title: Statistical learning
item.description:
Statistical learning#

Two words from statistics: average and variance#

The next slides use the symbols \(\mathbb E\) and \(\operatorname{Var}\). Many students last met them in a first-year statistics course, so they are defined here, with an example, before they are used.

Expected value (long-run average): \(\mathbb E(Z) \approx (z_1 + z_2 + \dots + z_m)/m\) for a large number of repeats \(m\)

A random quantity \(Z\) takes a different value each time it is measured. Its expected value is the average we would get if we measured it very many times. “Approximately” because the average of a finite number of repeats is only close to it.

item.title: Assessing model accuracy
item.description:
Assessing model accuracy#

Measuring the quality of fit: the mean squared error#

Mean squared error on the training data: \(\mathrm{MSE} = \frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n (y_i - \hat f(x_i))^2\)

The standard score for a regression model.

item.title: Classification
item.description:
Classification#

Classification: the error rate#

For categories the MSE makes no sense. Count the mistakes instead

“Faulty minus healthy” has no meaning, so we cannot square a difference.

Error rate (fraction of wrong labels): \(\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n I(y_i \neq \hat y_i)\)
